# Piora

> Piora is a community-maintained, open-source, local-first desktop workspace for the Pi agent runtime. It combines agent conversations, project files, Git, browser automation, multi-agent collaboration, scheduled tasks, and controlled HarmonyOS NEXT device automation in one interface.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/kexijiang/Piora
Latest release: https://github.com/kexijiang/Piora/releases/latest
License: MIT
Platforms: Windows 10/11 x64 and Linux x64
Relationship notice: Piora is independently maintained and is not affiliated with or representative of Pi, pi-web, OpenAI, or Codex.

## Product model

Piora reuses Pi's AgentSession, models, tools, skills, prompts, extensions, SettingsManager, and resource-loading model. It adds a modern desktop interface and local runtime services. A normal Session owns a conversation and agent runtime. A Room coordinates multiple Session-backed agents. Goal and Plan are execution modes implemented by first-party extensions. The right workspace exposes files, Git changes, browser state, commands, search, review, and Harmony devices.

## Complete capability index

### 1. Agent conversations and task execution

- Streaming chat with Markdown, GFM, syntax highlighting, math, Mermaid, images, tool calls, process output, and readable command results.
- Normal mode for iterative work; Target mode for persistent execution until verified completion or a concrete blocker; Plan mode for read-only inspection and a structured editable plan.
- Structured plan approval, dependency-ordered steps, evidence, artifacts, verification coverage, change summaries, and interrupted-run recovery.
- Steer a running task immediately or queue another instruction; stop active work at any time.
- Native structured user-input cards for single choice, multiple choice, and free-form replies.
- Context usage, compaction, session naming, system prompt editing, slash commands, and completion notifications.

### 2. Files and workspace

- Project file tree, indexed and fuzzy search, file tabs, and Source / Edit / Preview / Diff views.
- Text editing with line numbers, cursor position, Tab indentation, keyboard save, and draft preservation.
- Safe conflict handling for external disk changes; explicit continue, reload, or overwrite choices.
- Read-only previews for images, audio, PDF, DOCX, and Markdown; full-screen chat image viewer.
- File writes use allow-listed roots, path and symlink validation, size limits, SHA-256 versions, locks, and atomic replacement.
- Per-file change cards with added/removed line counts and expandable inline diffs.

### 3. Git and worktrees

- Git status, diffs, line statistics, branch listing, stage, unstage, commit, push, and explicit revert operations.
- Right-side change and review panels linked to the originating conversation workspace.
- Create, switch, list, and remove Git worktrees for parallel work. Dirty removal requires confirmation.

### 4. Built-in browser

- Desktop browser workspace with first-party agent browser tools.
- Tabs, address navigation, back/forward, refresh, screenshots, bookmarks, and downloads.
- Import Chrome bookmark bars while preserving useful folder hierarchy.
- Capability is discoverable in compatible agent sessions without changing profiles.

### 5. HarmonyOS NEXT device automation

- Discover official HDC runtimes from DevEco Studio, command-line tools, environment variables, or PATH.
- Discover USB devices, show a local live projection, read screenshots and UI trees, and inspect structured or raw logs.
- Tap, double tap, long press, swipe, fling, drag, input text, press keys, launch apps, and wait for UI or screen stability.
- Observe-act-verify loop returns fresh references and semantic state changes after actions.
- Optional dedicated vision model; raw screenshots are not forwarded across models by default.
- Exclusive device leases, serialized actions, stale-state checks, sensitive-action boundaries, and emergency stop.
- Does not bypass lock screens, CAPTCHAs, payments, system authorization, or app permissions.

### 6. Multi-agent Rooms and Agent Teams

- Persistent Rooms hold team identities, roles, responsibilities, messages, tasks, audit data, and artifact indexes.
- Agent roles include coordinator, planner, executor, reviewer, and participant. Stable identities can rebind to Sessions.
- Dependency-aware scheduling, concurrency limits, leases, bounded retries, evidence, artifacts, interruption recovery, and independent review.
- Questions, approvals, progress, and final results appear in Room chat.
- Managed shared workspace or a custom shared directory inside a member project root.
- Cross-project Session selection, @ mentions, message navigation, and responsive drawers.

### 7. Sessions, projects, and remote control

- Project-bound Sessions plus projectless Chat backed by a managed Piora workspace.
- Search, pin, rename, auto-name, archive, restore, duplicate, export, recoverable delete, independent fork, and in-session branch navigation.
- Lazy history loading and reconciliation after refresh, visibility changes, or network recovery.
- Local HTTP/SSE API for capability discovery, Session creation, messages, state, history, tools, steer, abort, events, and command status.
- Bearer capability tokens, Session allowlists, revocation, rate limiting, bounded JSON, and idempotency keys.

### 8. Models, authentication, and vision

- API keys, OAuth/device-code login, logout, provider status, and custom model definitions.
- Catalog discovery, connection tests, reasoning-level selection, and model-scope filtering.
- Explicit image-input capability per model.
- Optional visual-agent sidecar lets text-only primary models understand images through bounded observations.
- Original images remain local to the Session unless the selected image-capable model is intentionally used.
- Separate model preferences for visual understanding, automatic titles, and prompt optimization.

### 9. Extensions, Skills, Plugins, MCP, and prompts

- Unified extension inventory with precise enable/disable controls matching the actual Session load plan.
- Search, install, update-check, and enable/disable Skills.
- Install, remove, update, enable, disable, and inspect Plugin packages and packaged resources.
- Discover runtime MCP servers and cached tool capabilities without exposing credentials or tool input schemas.
- Slash commands, prompt resources, and first-party extension status are integrated into the chat UI.

### 10. Scheduled tasks and follow-ups

- Persistent RRULE and timezone-aware schedules, pause/resume, run now, missed-run recovery, bounded history, and notification policy.
- Chat heartbeats continue an existing conversation; project tasks create a fresh conversation for each run.
- Conversation task cards, Settings overview, and a complete right-side editor.
- The first-party automation tool is used only when the user explicitly asks for reminders, monitoring, follow-ups, or recurring work.

### 11. Appearance, companion pets, and input preferences

- Light, Dark, Midnight, Forest, and Dream Skin color themes.
- Twenty bundled original local WebP backgrounds with independent sidebar/workspace opacity, readability mask, and blur.
- Custom PNG, JPEG, WebP, or AVIF backgrounds are stored locally, preferably in IndexedDB, and are not uploaded.
- Font preferences, keyboard navigation, focus handling, resizable panels, and narrow-screen layouts.
- Optional companion pet shows Session state, TODOs, and click-to-send quick phrases. Declarative local pet assets can be imported after validation.
- Choose Enter or Ctrl+Enter to send and a default Steer or Queue behavior while a task runs.

### 12. Desktop delivery, updates, and local safety

- Windows installer, Windows portable EXE, Windows extract-and-run ZIP, and Linux x64 AppImage.
- Windows installer supports in-app update checks, release notes, download progress, and explicit install-and-restart.
- System tray, window-bounds restoration, dynamic localhost port, and a random desktop token per launch.
- Optional migration of the complete Pi data directory with validation, staged copy, atomic activation, and retained backup.
- No analytics SDK, ads, account service, or default telemetry.
- Render isolation, recoverable error screens, task-state reconciliation, and opt-in native completion notifications.

## Quick start

1. Download from the canonical latest-release URL. Windows beginners should choose the setup installer; Portable and ZIP are no-install options. Linux x64 users choose AppImage.
2. Open Settings > Models. Select a provider, authenticate with API key or OAuth when available, save, and run a connection test.
3. Choose a project folder for file/code work, or use the fixed Chat section for a projectless conversation.
4. Describe the desired outcome and verification, for example: "Inspect the login flow, fix the issue, run relevant tests, and summarize evidence."
5. Review files, diffs, and Git state in the right workspace. Use Steer to redirect active work or Queue to add the next instruction.

## Security and release notes

Public packages are currently unsigned. Download only from the canonical GitHub Releases page and compare the selected file against SHA256SUMS.txt. Piora has no default telemetry, but model requests, OAuth, model discovery, package installation, and third-party extensions may access networks according to the user's choices and provider policies.
